item.title: Barcelona reassess defensive targets as Lisandro Martinez falls down shortlist
item.description: Barcelona reassess defensive targets as Lisandro Martinez falls down shortlist Barcelona are considering several alternatives to Lisandro Martinez as they prepare to strengthen Hansi Flick’s defence, with Alessandro Bastoni, Finn Jeltsch, Nico Schlotterbeck and Ruud Nijstad all ahead of the Manchester United defender in their recruitment priorities. According to SPORT , the Catalan club is assessing different profiles in order to improve their defensive stability for the second half of the season. However, the club’s financial restrictions and the contractual situations of their preferred targets could make the recruitment process particularly complicated ahead of the January 2027 transfer window. Barcelona’s defensive recruitment a priority for Deco Barcelona have made considerable progress in rebuilding their squad, with Deco’s recruitment work and La Masia’s contribution helping the club develop a stronger group of players. However, central defence remains an area where the sporting department believes further investment is necessary, something that Deco agreed to recently . Given the injuries Barcelona have suffered this season, Flick needs defenders who can operate comfortably in a high defensive line, contribute to building attacks from the back and cope with the space left behind when Barcelona commit players forward. Deco and Flick are not in favour of signing Lisandro Martinez. (Photo by Michael Regan/Getty Images) Finding someone who can offer those qualities alongside Pau Cubarsi is therefore an important recruitment objective. The financial situation also means Barcelona cannot pursue the most attractive name on the market, meaning that player departures are as crucial as finding a new player. Four defensive targets, four different challenges At present, Bastoni remains an attractive option because of his experience at Inter Milan and his ability to progress possession from the back. Deco has previously explored the possibility of signing the Italian, although completing a deal during the middle of the season would be difficult. Jeltsch represents a different type of investment. The Stuttgart defender is under contract until 2030, and the Bundesliga club’s €60 million valuation makes negotiations challenging. Barcelona have Finn Jeltsch on their radar. (Photo by Christian Kaspar-Bartke/Getty Images) Schlotterbeck also presents contractual complications at Borussia Dortmund, while Nijstad is another emerging defensive prospect whose long-term contract with FC Twente could make his recruitment difficult. Simply put, neither club has an obvious financial incentive to negotiate a favourable mid-season departure. item.description: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - AUGUST 15: (L-R) Jon Anik, Joe Rogan, and Daniel Cormier pose for a photo prior to the UFC 330 event at Xfinity Mobile Arena on August 15, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Chris Unger/Zuffa LLC) Nearly a week after UFC 334 , we’re still dealing with the fallout of Ciryl Gane vs. Josh Hokit . Though Gane walked away with the first defense of his undisputed crown via unanimous decision (highlights here) , there are a lot of hot takes about the contest. Was it one of the best bouts of the year or a sloppy bar brawl? Should Gane have lost a point for the eye poke that the referee initially missed? Did Gane really deserve the decision or was Hokit robbed? Will there be an immediate rematch sometime next year? All Surprisingly, the controversy started before the bout was even halfway over. In the commentary booth, color commentators Daniel Cormier and Joe Rogan firmly disagreed about how the fight was playing out. Cormier thought it was clear that Gane was winning the early rounds despite Hokit’s pressure, whereas Rogan was adamant that Hokit was doing the better work. The judges ultimately sided with “DC,” but fans remain upset. There’s been significant backlash towards the former champion, including a petition that’s still picking up new signatures to this day. As the man in the middle, UFC’s head play-by-play commentator Jon Anik is now weighing in as well and defending his co-worker. “I understand a lot of people are coming at Daniel Cormier, and I would agree in some part that maybe he was too insistent on the broadcast that Ciryl Gane had won Rounds 1 and 2,” Anik said on his “Anik & Florian Podcast” (via MMA Junkie ). “I guess my issue is just that there’s just sort of a lot of venom, and I guess sort of anger out there when it comes to the fight and how it was scored. item.title: Golden boy back! Vincent Kompany backs Jamal Musiala to prove Bayern chiefs wrong after health and contract storm
item.description: FC Bayern München v FK Bodo/Glimt - UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD1 - Getty Images Sport Jamal Musiala is set to return to the Bayern Munich squad for Friday's Bundesliga clash against 1. FC Koln after two months on the sidelines. Amid intense scrutiny from club chiefs over his fitness and lucrative contract, head coach Vincent Kompany has fiercely praised the playmaker's resilience. Musiala ready for long-awaited squad return Jamal Musiala is poised to return to the Bayern Munich matchday squad for Friday's Bundesliga clash against 1. FC Koln following nearly two months out of action. Head coach Vincent Kompany confirmed on Thursday that the Germany international has recovered from a thigh muscle fibre tear sustained during international warm-ups in late September . "The way Jamal fights and what he's showing right now - I hope you'll all get to see more of it over the coming months and that he can demonstrate it on the pitch," Kompany said. "He's showing an incredible mentality and a real hunger. He'll probably be in the squad tomorrow." Standing firm amid boardroom scrutiny Musiala's return arrives during a turbulent period off the pitch, with honorary president Uli Hoeness recently questioning whether the 23-year-old can justify his reported €25 million annual salary following repeated health setbacks. Having also suffered neurological absence seizures during pre-season in August, Musiala has managed just four appearances so far in the 2026-27 campaign. Kompany, however, backed his star to emerge stronger from the ordeal, pointing to Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane as proof of what players can achieve in Munich. "When players like him go through a difficult spell, they can draw strength from it - both mentally and physically," Kompany stated. "When I arrived, he was a 'golden child'. Seeing how he's handling the whole situation now is something special. I hope that in six months' time, it'll be a completely different story." Positive updates on Luis Diaz and Alphonso Davies Alongside Musiala's impending comeback, Kompany delivered encouraging fitness bulletins regarding wingers Luis Diaz and full-back Alphonso Davies. While Friday's visit from Koln comes slightly too soon for Diaz, the Colombian international is nearing full availability. "Lucho is doing very well. He's had a good week. Tomorrow's still a bit too soon for him, but we'll be able to get him back in action within the next seven days," Kompany revealed, before adding a brief reassurance on Davies: "Phonzy will be fine; I can't say any more than that at the moment." Reinforcements arrive for crucial winter run Getting key stars back on the grass provides a timely boost for Kompany, who has also just returned from his own four-week medical absence. With Bayern sitting atop the Bundesliga as the only unbeaten team across Europe's top five leagues, Musiala's creativity will prove vital across eight fixtures before the winter break.

item.title: Andriy Shevchenko hits back at Mykhailo Mudryk as Ukraine legend makes 'baseless slander' claim over doping ban controversy
item.description: Andriy Shevchenko - Getty Images Ukraine legend Andriy Shevchenko has reacted furiously to allegations made by Tottenham winger Mykhailo Mudryk regarding a failed drugs test that stalled the winger’s career. The former AC Milan and Chelsea striker, now leading the Ukrainian Association of Football, has dismissed the claims as a "baseless slander" against the national federation. Row erupts over Mudryk's meldonium suspension The dispute stems from a positive test for meldonium that sidelined the 25-year-old Chelsea loanee from November 2024 until July 2026 . Although Mudryk initially received a four-year ban, the sanction was lifted after he accepted breaching anti-doping rules. Speaking on the YouTube channel Guest of Gordon , Mudryk blamed the national setup for his failed test , accused the UAF of leaking case details and delaying his return, and claimed Shevchenko offered little support. In response, the UAF president alleged that Mudryk's representatives had repeatedly asked the federation to find an employee to take the blame. Mudryk points the finger as Shevchenko hits back Addressing the saga, Mudryk insisted the banned substance could only have entered his system in Ukraine. "The environment, the situation in the Ukrainian national team," he said. "It should never have existed. I probably haven't said it publicly yet, but I'm saying it now. I had never heard of a drug like meldonium. It is a drug you can only get in Eastern Europe. It could only have got into my body in Ukraine. There is no such drug in England." He added that it "points to the fact it was in a national team camp", replying bluntly when asked if he blamed the national side: "Yes, exactly." Shevchenko swiftly rejected those allegations. "I want to express my position regarding Mykhailo Mudryk's accusations," he said. "Loud statements were made about the UAF and the Ukrainian national team. This is baseless slander against our people, who do their work honestly and professionally." Addressing the alleged push for a scapegoat, Shevchenko stressed that official inquiries cleared the federation. "Such a proposal contradicts the principles of our work," he said. "The accusations made by Mykhailo's representatives were not confirmed or substantiated by evidence after numerous investigations and checks. The investigation and the final settlement agreement with WADA and the English FA confirm this." item.title: Thomas Frank shares his feelings on Crystal Palace appointment
item.description: Thomas Frank shares his feelings on Crystal Palace appointment Thomas Frank Returns to Crystal Palace as Relegation Fight Begins Thomas Frank is back, and he sounds exactly like a man who has had enough time away to think clearly. Crystal Palace have appointed the 53-year-old on a two-and-a-half-year deal, and his first message was simple. He is refreshed, reflective and ready for another go in the Premier League. Palace need that. They are bottom of the table, short on momentum and heading into a survival battle that will demand clarity more than noise. Frank arrives after a bruising end to his previous spell at Tottenham, where he was dismissed in February, less than eight months after taking charge. He could have stayed away longer. He chose not to. Thomas Frank Embraces Palace Challenge There was no attempt to dress it up. Frank admitted the break had been enjoyable. He travelled to Japan and Australia, spent time in Denmark and relaxed with family and friends. As he put it, he had been “visiting friends and family, eating too well [and] drinking too much wine”. Photo IMAGO He had every reason to extend that time off too. “I was very aware I didn’t want to do anything in the summer. I put a statement out there, I needed more time,” he said. Then came the line that tells you where his head is now, “I can actually, honestly say I would have been fine if it was three, four, five, six, seven months more, because it’s good to be back in the circus, but it’s also unbelievably good not to be in, especially if you enjoy life, which I do.” Still, Palace convinced him. The club’s internal pitch clearly mattered. Frank singled out chairman Steve Parish, along with Matt Hobbs and Iain Moody, as key figures in persuading him this was the right job at the right time. Crystal Palace Need Fast Impact That matters because sentiment gets you nowhere at the bottom of the Premier League. Palace need points, quickly. Frank’s reign starts with a trip to Coventry City on Saturday, and there is no gentle easing-in period. The task is obvious, steady the team, sharpen the structure and lift belief. Frank also made it clear that his time out of football was not spent feeling sorry for himself. “If you don’t learn from any of your jobs, I don’t think you reflect, I don’t think you improve, and I don’t think you get better,” said Frank. “Of course there’s a lot of things I have been reflecting over. item.title: Liverpool receive Alex Scott update ahead of January window
item.description: Liverpool receive Alex Scott update ahead of January window Alex Scott Transfer Latest as Liverpool Track Bournemouth Midfielder Alex Scott is moving back into focus, for Bournemouth and for clubs circling around him. Chelsea tried in the summer and are expected to come again in January. Arsenal remain interested. Liverpool do too, and that part matters given who is now at Anfield. Scott has 18 months left on his Bournemouth deal. That changes the conversation. It does not force a sale, but it does sharpen the decision making. Renew him, sell him, or risk watching leverage slip away. That is where Bournemouth are. Liverpool Interest Makes Sense Liverpool want midfield depth and they want quality on the ball. Scott fits that brief. He is technically clean, sees passes early and plays with control. He also knows what Andoni Iraola wants. Scott was an important part of the coach’s setup at Bournemouth before Iraola left for Liverpool, so there is no mystery here about suitability. That does not mean a transfer is close. It means the logic is obvious. Liverpool know the player, the player knows the method, and the contract situation keeps this alive. Marco Rose Addresses Bournemouth Situation Marco Rose was direct when asked about the noise. “We talk everyday about football and about personal stuff. We have a good connection and we know how it works in this business. “Bournemouth is a top club for young players to improve. He is quite committed with the club and we can’t change the rumours. He is a Bournemouth player and he likes to be a Bournemouth player. The other things are not of interest to me as a coach.” That is what managers say when they want calm and would rather discuss availability than transfer chatter. Alex Scott Injury Return Comes at Good Time For now, the immediate issue is football. Scott is back after a hamstring problem that kept him out of four Premier League games. Rose confirmed he is ready to start, saying: “We have many games in the upcoming weeks, even next week three games, so a lot of choices and for sure he’s going to start in one of those games. “We have to increase his match time step by step. But he had a good two weeks with training and some rest and now I think Alex is ready, Junior is ready to get more match time and even to start.” After missing eight matches with a thigh injury, he returned to the squad for Bournemouth’s 2-1 win at Ipswich before the international break. The transfer talk can wait. His football cannot.

item.title: 'It was certainly a shock' - Vincent Kompany reveals honest truth behind four-week Bayern Munich absence
item.description: FBL-EUR-C1-BAYERN MUNICH-ARSENAL - AFP Vincent Kompany is officially back on the touchline for Bayern Munich ahead of Friday's Bundesliga clash against 1. FC Koln. After spending four weeks away recovering from a health scare, the Belgian coach has opened up on his medical tests, rival managers' support, and watching his side from home. Kompany returns to the Allianz Arena dugout Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany is back on the touchline ahead of Friday's Bundesliga clash against 1. FC Koln at the Allianz Arena. Having missed four weeks following a health scare caused by meningeal irritation, the 40-year-old welcomed his international players back to Sabener Strasse on Thursday after receiving full medical clearance . "I'm very grateful for the support I've received from the club and the doctors. I'm feeling really well again now and am delighted to be back with the team," Kompany said. "All the tests came back positive. I have to say, I'm in very good health; we've done lots of tests, all of which have come back clear." Admitting he ignored warning signs Kompany admitted his enforced break served as a wake-up call after he initially failed to listen to his body following an earlier Champions League tie against Arsenal. Despite the initial alarm, he thanked rival managers and his family for standing by him during his recovery. "I don't want to play it down; it was certainly a shock. But it was a result of me carrying on when I really should have taken a break," Kompany explained. "As well as my family, I'd also like to thank the coaching community. We're always competing against one another, but almost every coach has got in touch with me, even if we've played against each other and perhaps even had our differences." Praising his backroom staff from afar During his time away, Kompany stepped back completely from matchday decisions, trusting assistants Rene Maric, Aaron Danks, Floribert Ngalula and Daniel Fradley to maintain standards. Watching from home, he highlighted Bayern's fearless Champions League display against Atletico Madrid as a standout memory. "I didn't make any decisions," he noted. "When the head coach is absent, the handover has to be such that things carry on as they always do. They managed that very well. I really enjoyed the Atletico match. It was one of the finest moments of my coaching career, even though I wasn't there." Motivated for the pre-Christmas sprint Refreshed and armed with fresh tactical ideas gathered during his time off, Kompany is eager to lead Europe's last remaining unbeaten side in the top five leagues into a gruelling run of eight matches in 29 days. "There's one person at FC Bayern who is really motivated for this game against Koln. I've been waiting for four weeks," Kompany concluded. "If the players can sense my motivation, we'll have a good foundation for tomorrow's match."

What happened over a three-day run at the Players Era 8 tournament in Vegas won't stay in Vegas. These Cougars are for real. Just ask top-ranked Florida and No. 11 Kansas. The Cougars (6-0) completed a perfect trip to Sin City with a hold-on-to-your-seat 92-83 victory over the Jayhawks in the championship game at Michelob ULTRA Arena. In a week of chaos at the top of the national polls - with losses by No. 1 Florida, No. 2 Michigan State, No. 3 UConn and No. 5 Duke - the Cougars emerged as a legitimate national championship contender. item.title: Ducks "flat as a pancake" in shutout loss in Colorado
item.description: Nov 19, 2026; Denver, Colorado, USA; Colorado Avalanche center Brock Nelson (11) celebrates after his goal in the second period against the Anaheim Ducks at Ball Arena. DENVER – Joel Quenneville provided the most aptly succinct description of the Anaheim Ducks first shutout loss of the season. “We were flat as a pancake,” the Ducks coach said. Anaheim’s chronic defensive issues persisted following a competitive opening period, and the Ducks previously scalding hot offense was completely snowed under by the Colorado Avalanche in a sound defeat, 4-0, on Thursday at Ball Arena. Anaheim (11-11-1, 23 points) has lost four of its last five games following a five-game winning streak and has allowed four or more goals in 14 of its 23 games. “I think everything (was disconnected),” Jackson LaCombe said. “We turned too many pucks over. Just didn't have any jam on the offense. Throwing pucks away early. Didn't have any possession time. There’s things we’ve gotta fix.” Cutter Gauthier’s historically prolific 10-game goal streak came to a halt. Gauthier recorded just two shots and only one on the power play, as the Avalanche penalty kill rightly shaded his one-timer spot. Teemu Selanne maintains his hold on the longest goal streak in franchise history (11 games, 1997-98). All of Anaheim’s top performers were stagnant against Colorado, with Gauthier, Leo Carlsson, Beckett Sennecke and Mikael Granlund combining for three total shots. The Ducks spent an inordinate amount of time in their own defensive zone, as they again turned the puck over on their half of the ice, struggled on clears and couldn’t connect on clean breakouts. Stian Solberg, 2024 first-round pick, made his NHL debut, and with the 20-year-old Norwegian defenseman cracking the line-up, Anaheim iced a blue line with an average age of 22.67 years old. “Tough loss, but most fun game I ever played,” Solberg said. “It's cool to be out there on the biggest stage in the world. It's just something we've been kind of just looking at your whole life and when it finally happens, it's very special.” Nicolas Roy opened the scoring after an all-around failure by Anaheim on the opening draw of the second period. Beckett Sennecke couldn’t control the puck, fell at his own blue line, and the Avalanche pounced to send Roy walking around Lukáš Dostál, 1-0, eight seconds into the middle frame. Momentum continued to slide Colorado’s way, as Brock Nelson blasted a power-play one-timer three minutes later, 2-0. The Avalanche had the first three power plays of the night. Nelson netted another just under seven minutes later, as he toe-dragged around Jackson LaCombe and picked top glove on Dostál, 3-0. Another turnover ended up in the back of the Ducks net, as Devon Toews finished in the slot, 4-0, with just under 10 minutes to play. Dostál stopped 23 of 27 shots in his 12th start of the season and second in three games following a 6-2 loss to the New York Islanders on Saturday. Dostál stood in against numerous breakaways

item.title: Cowboys Could See Return of Injured Breakout Playmaker
item.description: Tyler Goodson #32 of the Dallas Cowboys Getty The Dallas Cowboys have delved into a good deal of drama this week, which is not where any NFL team wants its season to be after 10 weeks. But the Cowboys made their move with the demotion of defensive coordinator Christian Parker, following the 46-40 loss to the 49ers last Sunday, in which the team gave up 584 yards of offense and three plays that went for 66 yards on their own. Dallas made selling out to get to the quarterback a priority and while there was some success in that, the 49ers burned them enough times to make the whole enterprise of the Cowboys’ defense look futile. The issue has dominated news from The Star since, even as other issues have continues to crop up. One of them is backup running back Tyler Goodson. No doubt, Goodson had been one of the positive additions to the roster–one of the few–this season, signed to be the backup running back after an injury to Malik Davis and the release of Emari Demercado. Before he was injured against the Colts in Week 9, Goodson had racked up 77 yards on 12 carries, and ran for 163 yards on 40 carries for the season. Cowboys May Get Tyler Goodson Back But the good news came down on Thursday amid the wreckage of the past week in Frisco: All is not lost on Goodson. He has sprains to both his PCL and MCL, but assuming the Cowboys stay in the playoff hunt, there is a strong chance we see Goodson again in 2026. According to Patrik Walker of the Cowboys website, there is hope on Goodson. 📰 update: Tyler Goodson suffered a sprained MCL and PCL against the Colts, I’m told. the goal for him, right now, is to return this season — the bye week (+rehab progress) plays a part in that discussion.he’s moving around better every day. #Cowboys pic.twitter.com/5EKUkbHhV5 — Patrik [No C] Walker (@VoiceOfTheStar) November 19, 2026 He wrote: “Update: Tyler Goodson suffered a sprained MCL and PCL against the Colts, I’m told. the goal for him, right now, is to return this season — the bye week (+rehab progress) plays a part in that discussion. “he’s moving around better every day.” Dallas does not have a bye week until Week 14, the week of December 14. Coach Brian Schottenheimer was a big booster of his before he went down with the knee injury. He said of Goodson: “I think at the end of the day when you look at we’re rebuilding the room a little bit, the injury to Malik was something that we hated to see happen. Tyler was a guy that we had some love for at the cutdown spot. item.title: Ineos’ heavy-handed approach with fans shows no sign of letting up in latest punishment meted out
item.description: Ineos’ heavy-handed approach with fans shows no sign of letting up in latest punishment meted out Manchester United fans have had a lot to say so far this season. After a poor start to the season which has seen the club fall into the relegation zone, standards at the club are hitting depths they haven’t in decades. What’s more, fans are not only furious with their players’ performances but also with the state of the club’s ownership. Ineos’ poor decorum Since taking over football responsibilities at the club in 2024, Ineos have made many unpopular calls. They have scrapped reduced ticketing for children in 2024 and consecutively hiked up ticket prices in spite of a cost of living crisis. In addition, they have treated numerous fans incredibly badly amongst accusations of ticket touting. They have also forced many long-standing season ticket holders out of their seats to make room for more corporate seating in a show of disdain for the lifeblood of the football club. Latest issue As a result, United protested against the owners during the match against AS Roma in the Champions League and also versus Aston Villa just before the international break. item.description: Australia captain Pat Cummins found himself surrounded by reporters outside his home on Thursday as questions about the 2018 Sandpapergate scandal resurfaced. The incident returned to the headlines after former Australia batter Cameron Bancroft claimed that the entire team knew about the ball-tampering incident, contradicting Cummins' recent statement that he had no knowledge of it. A video of the incident has gone viral on social media, showing Cummins being approached by several journalists as he appeared to leave for training. When one reporter apologised for entering his premises, the Australian captain responded sharply, saying, "You're probably not that sorry". Cummins refused to answer questions about Bancroft's allegations, including whether he felt his former teammate had thrown him under the bus and whether the controversy could put his captaincy at risk. item.title: Donald Trump Pardons Pete Rose, but Baseball Legend’s Hall of Fame Fate Remains Open
item.description: Photo Credit: Win McNamee/Getty Images News via Getty Images Pete Rose has received a presidential pardon from Donald Trump , but the move does not settle his place in baseball history. Trump announced the decision more than two years after the former Cincinnati Reds star died. Why Pete Rose’s presidential pardon does not guarantee Hall of Fame induction Donald Trump announced the pardon on Truth Social , calling Rose a “true Baseball SUPERSTAR & LEGEND.” The president did not spell out its full scope in the post. Rose’s criminal case involved tax offenses, while his exclusion from baseball stemmed from gambling on games involving the Cincinnati Reds (via The Guardian ). Rose’s legal troubles added another blow in April 1990, when he admitted guilt on two charges involving fraudulent tax filings. He acknowledged hiding $354,968 in earnings across a four-year period. The court handed him a five-month prison sentence, and he later paid the IRS $366,042. The tax case followed his acceptance of a lifetime ban from Major League Baseball just months earlier. Rose’s betting scandal hinged on wagers he placed on the Reds while serving as both a player and manager between 1985 and 1987. MLB handed him a lifetime ban in 1989, shutting the door on his Hall of Fame hopes for decades. At the time, Rose acknowledged his wrongdoing, saying, “I know I’m not a bad person, but I did make some mistakes.” His eligibility changed in May 2025, when MLB Commissioner Rob Manfred ruled that permanently ineligible players would have their status restored after death. The decision affected 17 people, including Rose and Shoeless Joe Jackson. However, the Hall of Fame operates separately from MLB, and reinstatement does not guarantee election. item.title: Moore eyes Kane shirt as Spurs' past and future stars meet
item.description: Moore is Tottenham's youngest-ever Premier League player, having made his debut for the club's senior side at just 16 years old. [Getty Images] Cologne loanee Mikey Moore says he hopes to exchange shirts with former Tottenham team-mate Harry Kane when they face Bayern Munich in the Bundesliga on Friday. The 19-year-old England Under-21 international is on a season-long loan from Spurs, while Three Lions captain and Ballon d'Or winner Kane left north London to join Bundesliga giants Bayern in 2023. "I haven't actually spoken to him. When he was leaving Tottenham I was just coming into the first team so we don't really know each other too well," said Moore. "But we've got Bayern on Friday so I'm looking forward to hopefully getting a chat with him and maybe his top." The 19:30 GMT kick-off will be shown live on BBC Sport and iPlayer. Kane was still at Tottenham when Moore was first invited to train with the senior squad during the 2021-22 season. "He's been a massive idol of mine since I was really young," Moore told the Euro Leagues podcast last month. "When I first went up to train with the first team under Antonio Conte, Harry Kane was over there, and [I saw] some finishing that [I have] never seen anything like again. "It will be a great experience to play against him and share a pitch with him." The pair may not have crossed paths in Germany yet but Moore did bump into the England skipper while on international duty last month. "I'll try my best to get my hands on that shirt," Moore added. "I saw him on the last international break, actually, and went and said hello. "Hopefully, I'll be coming back to Koln with that in my hand." 'I wanted to take myself a little bit out of my comfort zone' Moore says the success of Jadon Sancho and Jude Bellingham in the Bundesliga influenced his decision to join Cologne on loan. Moore's move came almost a decade after a 17-year-old Sancho left Manchester City to join Borussia Dortmund. During his time in Germany, Sancho established himself as one of Europe's most exciting wingers, making more than 150 appearances for Dortmund and helping the club win the DFB-Pokal in 2021. He subsequently secured a £73m move to Manchester United. Bellingham followed a similar path in 2020, leaving boyhood club Birmingham City to join Dortmund. The midfielder quickly developed into one of the most sought-after players in world football before joining Real Madrid for an initial £88.5m in 2023. "Over the years you've seen so many young players come out here, and there are good examples of world-class players like Jude Bellingham and Jadon Sancho doing really well," Moore said. "It's a really attractive place to play football, especially for a young attacker. It's a great platform to play, and that was sold to me by the people at the club and the manager. "They've put real trust in me, and the amount of game time I've played so quickly in my Koln [Cologne] career has been nice. It's been good to have that trust from all the staff

item.title: Broncos Star’s $67 Million Contract Could Set Market for Giants Starter
item.description: Denver Broncos cornerback Riley Moss. Getty The biggest reason the Denver Broncos have become one of the NFL’s elite teams over the last three seasons is the hiring of head coach Sean Payton and his ability to work with George Paton on making sure the talented players they have on their roster stay on their roster — mainly thanks to primo savings by not letting them hit the open market in free agency. The Broncos were at it again on Thursday, signing cornerback Riley Moss to a 4-year, $67 million contract extension — about $16.75 million per season to keep him in Denver until 2030. As the Broncos’ CB2 at outside cornerback opposite NFL All-Pro Patrick Surtain, it could set the market for that tier of player. It’s also a deal that likely caught the New York Giants‘ attention, who could face a similar decision with cornerback and 2023 1st-round pick Deonte Banks. “$16.75M/year for a CB2,” The Athletic’s Dan Duggan wrote on his official X account on Thursday. “Greg Newsome got $15.25M. Data points to keep in mind for Deonte Banks’ negotiations.” It likely ends up being a steal for the Broncos — something the Giants should keep in mind. In a best-case scenario, Moss could have hit free agency with a value of around $20 million per year. Over the lifetime of the contract, that’s big savings. Giants Spent Big at Cornerback in Free Agency The Giants spent big at cornerback in free agency before the 2025 season, signing Paulson Adebo to a 3-year, $54 million contract. After a rocky first year, Adebo lost his starting job to Banks in training camp before the 2026 season — the same Banks who was a 1st-round pick in 2023 by the Giants but was essentially written off by the last coaching staff. “If the depth chart is legit, my god … Paulson Adebo, how did you lose a starting job to Deonte Banks!!!” Empire State Media’s Alex Wilson wrote on his official X account. “I’m excited to see if Banks turns things around, but man, what a colossal waste of money on Adebo if true.” The truth about Banks is that he’s made himself a ton of money this year — he’s always been one of the fastest players in the league, and showing he can be a reliable, full-time starter was the final step. The Giants might be smart to offer him something slightly less than what the Broncos offered Moss to see if he’ll bite — start at a 4-year, $50 million offer and be willing to go up to $60 million if needed. MINNEAPOLIS — Karl-Anthony Towns’ old coach has seen the full journey. Chris Finch heard all the criticism Towns constantly received during his Timberwolves tenure. “Particularly when he started his playoff journey,” Finch said before the Knicks’ 102-99 win over the Timberwolves on Thursday night, “how much flak he had gotten.” Towns returned to Minnesota for the third time since the blockbuster trade with the Knicks two years ago, recording 22 points, 12 rebounds and four assists in the win. It was his first time returning as an NBA champion. Timberwolves head coach Chris Finch speaks on the sideline as guard Bones Hyland looks on during a Nov. 16, 2026, in Minneapolis. AP Photo/Ellen Schmidt He is no longer the oft-criticized star many saw as an underperformer and contract albatross. Towns now is playing some of the best basketball of his career after playing a central role in the Knicks’ championship. He has shed a lot of the narratives that plagued him as a pro. Finch enjoyed watching it from afar. “It was fun to see him at the heart of it, too,” Finch said. “Especially as they were kind of tweaking their offense going along and all of his skills came to the surface through that.” Towns called it “bittersweet” returning as a champion, having wanted to deliver a title to the organization with which he spent his first nine years. Karl-Anthony Towns shoots over center Rudy Gobert during the Knicks’ 102-99 win over the Timberwolves on Nov. 19, 2026, in Minneapolis. This is the last place that I got to play basketball with my mom. I got to see the kids be young before now. Jolani, my niece, who was in my Rookie of the Year photo actually in here, she was a baby, and now she’s in high school. It’s a different part of life, but it’s a part of life that I really enjoy.” Head coach Mike Brown said his team’s hustle allowed it to escape with a win. “The thing that saved us was winning the 50-50 ballgame,” Brown said. “We were 13-for-14 in that area, and that was huge for us because we had trouble scoring in the fourth.”

item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Eastern Conference Most notably, Nashville SC set a new MLS regular season points record after dispatching Cincinnati this afternoon.
